item.title: Purple wave, blue wave: Valkyries parade doubles as election celebration
item.description: Valkyries' mascot Violet waves to fans in attendance to see the 2026 WNBA Champions at Jack London Square in Oakland, Calif. on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Following the ceremony, the team will bring the WNBA Championship Trophy across the Bay to San Francisco for the parade. (Yalonda M. James/S.F. Chronicle) Giddy energy from Tuesday night's Democratic electoral sweep seemed only to grow Wednesday morning as revelers gathered for the Valkyries WNBA championship parade. That much was clear from the sign that Serena Poon held aloft as she stood on the ferry lawn at Jack London Square, where the players and their entourage would soon depart by boat to San Francisco. "Purple wave 10/31; Blue wave 11/2," it said, linking the team's come-from-behind victory on Halloween night to a national blowout by Democrats, one so overwhelming that pundits ran out of tidal metaphors to describe it. The connection seemed fitting when a procession of Democratic politicians strode down the Embarcadero to welcome the Valkyries players when their boat was set to dock near the Ferry Building at noon. Among the delegation: Sen. Adam Schiff, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, state Sen. Scott Wiener (who is now leading in the race to succeed Pelosi) and Mayor Daniel Lurie in a violet shirt. For Poon, the political contact high was palpable. "We're just riding the high of Valks win, and then last night was just historic with blue wave," she said. "It was like a blue tsunami, and I'm just so stoked." Every Embarcadero-bound BART train and Muni bus became a purple and black menagerie as fans flocked in with jerseys, feathery boas and birdlike headdresses. If the attire seemed apolitical, the placards were not. Beth Jaeger of San Francisco arrived at the Embarcadero at 8 a.m. dressed as a Valkyrie, complete with purple face paint - and a sign that said "In a world of Sophies, be a Gabby." The slogan referenced public comments by Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who has insisted that trans women should be barred from the WNBA. Henry, from Oakland, holds a sign celebrating both the Valkyries' championship and Democrats' sweeping wins in Tuesday's midterm election. (Saul Pink / S.F. Chronicle) On the back of Jaeger's sign: "Welcome to the Gay Area." Others echoed pro-LGBTQ messages that, while not directly tied to an election wedge issue on Tuesday, generally defied the Trump Administration's stances on gender politics and diversity. As the morning wore on, "Gay Area" logos proliferated along the Embarcadero: in shimmery ink on card stock, emblazoned on T-shirts, embroidered on denim jackets, scrawled onto decals. "It was already so hopeful to see them win, and then to see and then to see so much hope across the country," said Cat De La Pena of San Jose, dangling her own hand-made "Gay Area" sign with a portrait of Valkyries forward and championship MVP Gabby Williams, arms outstretched to sink a 3-pointer into the basket. item.title: Dianna Russini reportedly returning to sports media ‘next week’
item.description: Credit: The Dan Patrick Show Dianna Russini has apparently kept herself on the sidelines long enough. The former top NFL insider for The Athletic who became embroiled in scandal this offseason after numerous photos surfaced showing her cozy and seemingly intimate relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is set to return “next week” according to a report by Mike Florio in Pro Football Talk . “Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she’ll be returning to work ‘next week,'” Florio reports, indicating that it is “unclear” for what outlet she’ll be working for, or what job she will be doing. Russini resigned from The Athletic in April, one week after the New York Post published the first batch of photos showing her and Vrabel together at a high-end resort in Arizona. In her letter of resignation, Russini maintained that there was no foul play between her and Vrabel. “Rather than allowing this [scandal] to continue, I have decided to step aside now – before my current contract expires on June 30. I do so not because I accept the narrative that has been constructed around this episode, but because I refuse to lend it further oxygen or to let it define me or my career,” Russini wrote at the time. Last month, the New York Post reported that Russini had hired crisis management expert Melissa Nathan , one of the first signs that the veteran NFL reporter was eyeing a return to media. Russini has not made any public statements since her resignation in April. Whether Russini will return in a capacity that relies on her credibility as a reporter, or in a role that is more personality-focused, is unclear. No doubt, Russini maintains a large rolodex of contacts throughout the league, though those sources’ willingness to speak candidly with her might be compromised after the scandal. Russini has long been able to hold court in more casual settings, however, and would likely command an audience even without dishing out NFL scoops. item.title: Joe Scarborough goes after ESPN’s Pat McAfee: ‘It is a shame for the viewer’
item.description: Pat McAfee is a problem for ESPN’s “College GameDay,” Joe Scarborough of “Morning Joe” hammered away at Tuesday during election day. item.title: Meet the Shasta Family YMCA Athletes of the Week winners for Oct. 25-31
item.description: Two Shasta County athletes are being recognized for their outstanding achievements on the field and court. This week, Foothill and Redding Christian high school athletes are being highlighted. Turner Knowles, Foothill Sport : Football School : Foothill Class : Senior Team Contributions : Foothill running back Turner Knowles had a career day in a wild Week 9 win over Enterprise. item.title: Brewers Should Avoid Signing Jake Bauers To Multi-Year Deal
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers Jake Bauers had a breakout season at 30 years old, and the Milwaukee Brewers extended him the qualifying offer. If Bauers accepts his one-year, $23.15 million offer, the Brewers don't have any choice to make. He will be back at that price. However, after the year he had, he should have a couple of multi-year offers on the table as well. The Brewers do not need to be one of the teams making one of those offers. Having Bauers back for one season would be great, because if he is unable to replicate his career year, they would be clear of him. There is a chance that his 2026 season ends up being something like Trent Grisham's 2025 season. Every team will need to decide whether they believe Bauers has finally figured out the big leagues with his new approach to the game or if last season was a fluke. The rest of the league may let the Brewers be the team that has to figure it out by making Bauers accept the qualifying offer. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! As far as keeping Bauers past next season, the Brewers have no need to. Not only do they have Andrew Fischer, Blake Burke and Luke Adams capable of playing first base knocking on the door of the big leagues, but they also have Andrew Vaughn who could be a potential option past next season. Bauers will be expensive to keep on a multi-year deal, and could really block some prospects the team views fondly. The Brewers should not change the way they do business just because they won the World Series. Bauers was a great player for them, and his efforts won't be forgotten. Ultimately, bringing him back for one more year won't hurt their long-term plans, and it will minimize the damage if his breakout proves to be a fluke. item.title: As Greg Schiano’s future hangs in balance, Rutgers fans have minds made up: ‘We need a change’
item.description: SHI Stadium was half-empty as Rutgers hosted a Big Ten blueblood, but those who made the trek to Piscataway made their voices heard. There were loud, sustained boos following a controversial call from the officials. There was a jubilant celebration as the final minutes of a close game ticked off the clock. There were frequent chants to fire an underperforming coach. The problem for the Scarlet Knights : all of that noise came from the visiting Michigan fans. Along with a 28-21 win on the field , the Wolverines (5-3, 2-3) blew out Rutgers (2-6, 1-4) in the stands on Saturday. Rutgers +17.5 point spread is currently sitting at -116 on ProphetX for Saturday’s Big Ten clash versus Michigan. Also, view our helpful guide to the best sportsbook promos to shop for competitive odds. Michigan fans made up at least half of a crowd that was announced at 39,540, the lowest official attendance at SHI Stadium for a non-COVID Big Ten game since head coach Greg Schiano returned in the 2020 season. Despite their team stumbling through a mediocre season, Michigan fans brought plenty of life into a moribund building. Rutgers fans, meanwhile, spoke with their absence. “I really don’t worry about things I can’t control,” Schiano said following the game. “I have enough of my own issues that I have to work on. I just try to do that. As I’ve always told you guys, I’m grateful for the ones that came, because those people, they’re supporting us through thick and thin. We’ve had thick here and we’re a little bit thin right now.” Two years removed from reaching a second straight bowl game and appearing to be on an upward trajectory, the Scarlet Knights are barreling toward their worst record of Schiano’s second stint after going 5-7 last fall. After getting upset by UMass , beaten by Boston College , fall short against USC and get blown out by Northwestern and Indiana — with wins over FCS Howard and last-place Maryland in between — Rutgers will need to win two of their final four games to match the 4-8 mark of the 2022 season. They are projected to be underdogs in their next three games (at Wisconsin, vs. Nebraska, at Penn State). Rutgers has one of the worst defenses in the country again , and despite having two of the best skill players in college football in wide receiver KJ Duff and running back Antwan Raymond, its offense is mediocre, ranking 73rd nationally in points per game. The Scarlet Knights, who are 7-13 overall since the start of the 2025 season, have lost their last four Big Ten home games and they are 3-9 in their last 12 conference games in Piscataway. They have lost 24 of their last 28 games as underdogs of more than a field goal , have not defeated a ranked opponent in 17 years and have not been ranked in 14 years. item.title: Could Queen City Quarter become an everyday destination in Uptown Charlotte?
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets are part of an ownership group that purchased the former EpiCentre complex in Uptown Charlotte, now known as Queen City Quarter, for $27.5 million. The purchase price covers a property with an estimated value of nearly $100 million. Sports analysts consider the three-company venture well financed. Erik Spanberg, a reporter with the Sports Business Journal, noted that the acquisition follows earlier municipal approvals for facility upgrades. “I don’t think many of us knew that the Charlotte Hornets were going to be part of the buying group,” Spanberg said. He added that “it started when the city approved the arena renovations and the training center,” explaining that “teams want to surround their arenas and stadiums with things that they develop and own.” PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Former EpiCentre site Queen City Quarter undergoes major change Rick Schnall, co-owner of the Charlotte Hornets, hinted in May that broader developments were being considered alongside basketball facilities. “From the beginning, this project is more than it is not just about basketball,” Schnall said. “It’s about continuing momentum in Uptown Charlotte in the city of Charlotte and strengthening the Spectrum Center and the community around it.” Other NBA franchises have pursued similar arena-adjacent real estate projects. In 2015, the Sacramento Kings entered a joint venture to redevelop a plaza into 1 million square feet of space known as Downtown Commons, or DOCO, surrounding the Golden one Center. According to the developer, that project influenced $6.7 billion in new projects by 2022, while bringing 150 retail businesses, residential units, hotels, restaurants, and increased foot traffic to the area. Spanberg noted that multiple franchises have executed comparable development projects around their venues. “In the NBA, you’ve seen not only Sacramento, but you’ve also seen Milwaukee Bucks do it really well with the beer district. You’ve seen the Indiana Pacers do it recently,” Spanberg said. He added that the long-term challenge for such projects lies in sustained activity. “The question always is, can you do it to an extent where people want to come not just on game day, but every day,” Spanberg said. Similar developments are also underway elsewhere in North Carolina. A new entertainment district is planned in Raleigh surrounding the Lenovo Center. According to the Sports Business Journal , those plans feature thousands of housing units, dining areas, and an enhanced tailgating experience for Carolina Hurricanes fans.

item.description: Wisconsin head coach Luke Fickell leads his team to the field before their game against Notre Dame Sunday, September 6, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Wisconsin Badgers were embarrassed 30-0 by the Iowa Hawkeyes in yet another rivalry game flop, as they fell to 5-3 on the season and 3-2 in conference play. It was a game where Wisconsin lost on every side and was awfully reminiscent of the team’s previous two losses to Iowa. Luke Fickell has now been outscored 124-16 in his four games at Wisconsin against Iowa. After the game, Fickell spoke with the media, outlining his frustrations and sharing his thoughts on the game. Here’s everything he said after the loss on Saturday. Opening Statement Well, that’s an old-fashioned ass whooping, and it doesn’t feel good. Were we prepared? Were we not prepared? We didn’t play like we were prepared today. They asked me if there were any positives, and I said I don’t know that I could find any positives in the way that we played, the way we performed. Yeah, they kept battling no matter what, but that’s a foregone conclusion. You have to do that. It’s, do you battle with the intent? Do you have the intensity to understand what it’s going to be like when you walk into this place and what you have to do in order to not just win, but make this a game? And we did none of that today. It’s very, very disappointing. I’m not sitting here saying I’ve got any answers for you. I’m not pointing any fingers at anybody because all three phases of the game, we were completely manhandled for 60-plus minutes. On why this keeps happening vs. Iowa… I don’t know. We made an overemphasis on it in the past, on the rivalry and what we needed to be able to do all of spring football and all of winter and all of fall. And then this year, it’s like, look, let’s make sure we understand, we respect the rivalry, but we don’t overdo something that is going to put us in a position where we play too emotional and can’t play 60-plus minutes. And we didn’t do that either. I think first of all, you’ve got to win the line of scrimmage. And I know that we can honestly say for the last couple years, we have not done that. And so anything beyond that, there’s a lot of other things, but that’s where it starts and that’s where it has been. On whether Iowa’s recent dominance has affected Wisconsin’s confidence in the rivalry… No, I don’t. There’s so many guys here that don’t even know or understand what’s happened the last couple years. We explained it and talked about it and went through some of those things, but they didn’t live it. So it’s not like they have some shell shock of some remembrance of what has happened. I don’t think that’s the case. It’s just the sheer fact that we didn’t play today. Whether there’s an arrogance and a delusion coming off of last week that we felt like we were in a different place, I hope we have more maturity than that. But surely it didn’t look like it today. item.title: Weather-hit Eden Gardens clash: Maharashtra put Bengal under pressure after reducing them to 76/4
item.description: KOLKATA: Weather continued to play spoilsport as Maharashtra enjoyed an upper hand in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group ‘C’ clash with Bengal at Eden Gardens here on Wednesday. The visitors will fancy their chances after reducing Bengal to 76/4 in the second innings, overall just one run ahead of Maharashtra’s first-innings total of 218, at stumps on Day III. Only 27.5 overs were bowled in the three hours and 16 minutes of play on the penultimate day which started after the whole first session was washed out due to rain. Maharashtra enjoyed a 75-run lead after their first innings ended in the fourth over of the morning, with 11 runs added to their overnight total of 207/9, when overnight unbeaten Pradeep Dadhe was trapped in front by Mohammed Shami for 27. Tanay Sanghvi remained unbeaten on 60 that came off 179 deliveries with the help of three boundaries and one six. Shami finished with 4/37 while Shahbaz Ahmed took 3/39. The Bengal second innings unfolded much like their first essay, with skipper Abhimanyu Easwaran the first to depart, chasing an away-going ball from Dadhe and being caught by wicketkeeper Saurabh Nawale in the fifth over of their innings. Sanghvi was in the thick of action when he bagged Sudip Gharami and Sudip Chatterjee in a gap of three deliveries to reduce Bengal to 25/3 just five overs later. Gharami played one on the rise and was caught at gully by Digvijay Patil for 12 while Chatterjee was trapped in front trying to play across the line without scoring. Opener Ankur Paul and Abishek Porel were involved in a 49-run fourth-wicket stand but did not look very convincing as Maharashtra skipper Prithvi Shaw set up an attacking field. The ploy did pay dividends as Paul was caught at silly point by Patil off left-arm spinner Hitesh Walunj for 32. Suraj Singh Jaiswal joined Porel as the duo was able to erase the deficit when bad light once again stopped play at tea after an extended second session of play. An outright win for Maharashtra will help them join Bengal at the top with 18 points while Bengal will look to save the match and return with one point, which will keep them as the sole leaders of the group.

item.title: ESPN analyst rips College Football Playoff committee over Ohio State, Indiana rankings
item.description: ESPN’s Greg McElroy had a big problem with the way the College Football Playoff handled a couple of Big Ten teams on Tuesday during the first CFP pole reveal. “I think the most confusing decision right now is that Indiana is at 4 and Ohio State is at 12,” the former Alabama quarterback said. “If we ask Hunter Yurachek and we say, ‘Hey, is Julian Sayin’s injury factoring in here?’ If he says, yes, then I can live with that. I understand that. They have applied a precedent with that in the past with Florida State and Jordan Travis.” Heather Dinich called the Hoosiers the biggest surprise of the night, but McElroy was on the roll. “And Indiana, if you watched them play against Michigan and then again against Minnesota, didn’t pass the eye test,” she said. “Josh Hoover was benched. If you look at the nonconference schedule, it is one of the weakest among all of these contenders. McElroy didn’t hold back. “But what I’m struggling with that is that we are in an era where we are trying to value strength of schedule. We’re trying to value strength of record. We’re encouraging people to play this difficult non-conference schedule. Ohio State put it all on the line in Austin, Texas in Week 2. All on the line. They went out there and lost a close game. A game in which they actually had a lot of control over. They give up 21 points in the fourth quarter, and they lose the game. “You remove that game. You put them up against North Texas, that’s who Indiana played. You put them against North Texas, they win that game convincingly. Now, you are looking at an Ohio State team that is 7-1 and Indiana team that is 8-1. And Ohio State has the head to head. Yet, there’s eight spots between them.” The Hoosiers lost 19-15 to Ohio State on Oct. 17 and their past three victories all came by seven points or less, including overtime victories against Michigan and Minnesota the past two weeks. The Hoosiers didn’t play a Power Four nonconference opponent (North Texas, FCS program Howard and Western Kentucky) and they haven’t yet defeated a team that’s ranked by the committee. “These are the people that are trying to tell us we want to schedule tough teams,” McElroy said. “Exhibit A: Why would we? “You have a fourth-ranked team right now that hasn’t played anyone in the non-conference in multiple years, eight spots ahead of the team that beat them on the field.” Yurachek said that comparing teams only happens when the teams are in the same pod. “We never got to the point where we were comparing Indiana to Ohio State in their head to head,” the CFP committee chair said. item.title: Tonya Harding Will Make Figure Skating Return 32 Years After Scandal: ‘I Just Can’t Walk Away’
item.description: Jaxon / MEGA Tonya Harding will return to the ice. The former figure skater, who will turn 56 next week, is preparing for a public skating show called “ Tonya and Friends ,” which will be held December 12 at Mountain View Ice Arena in Vancouver, Washington. “The love of skating is the reason why I’ve always come back,” Harding told KOIN 6 News in an interview published October 29. “I just can’t walk away from it.” However, the former Olympian did step back from competitive skating following her involvement in a scandal that shocked the sports world. Larry Burton / UPI Photo Service/Newscom/The Mega Agency More than 32 years ago, Harding pleaded guilty to conspiracy to hinder prosecution in connection with the assault on her U.S. skating rival, Nancy Kerrigan . The attack was orchestrated by Harding’s ex-husband, Jeff Gillooly , and others. Harding was banned from the U.S. Figure Skating Association for life following the scandal, and though she won the U.S. Championships in 1994, she was later stripped of her title. Xavier Collin/Image Press Agency / MEGA Harding competed as a professional boxer in the early 2000s. When it comes to her upcoming event, Harding told KOIN 6 News, “I just want people to come out and have fun and be able to enjoy a real skating show.” According to the outlet, Harding has been skating twice a week since the spring, and she is practicing jumps and spins while also building back her strength. “It makes my heart feel good,” she said. “And I am really glad people can come see me skate again.” Two coaches, including Dody Teachman , are helping her prepare for her return to the ice. “She’s a force all her own,” Teachman said.
